title: Initial Connection Failed
shortDescription: Kasa app could not establish a connection to the plug.
fullDescription:
During first setup, the phone must temporarily join the plug's own Wi-Fi (SSID starts with TP-LINK_Smart Plug). If the handoff fails or Private Wi-Fi Address is enabled, setup aborts.

Disable Private Wi-Fi Address for the setup SSID and retry.

fixSteps.title: Disable Private Wi-Fi Address
fixSteps.instruction: iPhone Settings > Wi-Fi > (i) on SSID > turn off Private Wi-Fi Address.

fixSteps.title: Disable cellular
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off mobile data during setup.

fixSteps.title: Retry setup
fixSteps.instruction: Restart Kasa app and add device again.

videoSearchQuery: Kasa smart plug connection failed setup

faq.a: For setup yes; local control works offline.

title: Kasa Requires 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi
shortDescription: Setup selected a 5 GHz network; not supported.
fullDescription:
Kasa smart plugs only support 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. Combined SSIDs (same name for 2.4 and 5) often cause phones to connect on 5 GHz during setup.

Separate SSIDs temporarily or connect the phone to the 2.4 GHz band only.

causes.cause: Router uses band-steering with same SSID

fixSteps.title: Split SSIDs
fixSteps.instruction: In router settings, give 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz different names.

fixSteps.title: Connect phone to 2.4 GHz
fixSteps.instruction: Join the 2.4 GHz SSID during setup.

faq.q: Can I rejoin combined SSID after setup?
faq.a: Yes, once paired you can recombine the bands.

title: Device Not Found During Setup
shortDescription: App scan does not see the plug's setup SSID.
fullDescription:
The plug broadcasts a setup SSID only in AP mode. If it is already provisioned or did not enter AP mode, no SSID is advertised.

Hold the button 5-10 seconds until the LED alternates amber/green to force AP mode.

fixSteps.title: Force AP mode
fixSteps.instruction: Hold button 5-10 seconds until LED blinks amber/green.

title: Final Setup Step Failed
shortDescription: Plug received credentials but could not connect to Wi-Fi.
fullDescription:
The plug copied the SSID and password but failed to associate. Usually due to a password typo, MAC filtering on the router, or weak signal at the plug location.

Power-cycle the plug and verify Wi-Fi credentials.
symptoms: Plug does not appear in device list

fixSteps.title: Verify password
fixSteps.instruction: Re-enter Wi-Fi password, watch for case sensitivity.

fixSteps.title: Check router filtering
fixSteps.instruction: Disable MAC filtering or add the plug MAC.

fixSteps.title: Move closer to router
fixSteps.instruction: Test setup near the router first.

faq.q: Is MAC filtering really blocking me?
faq.a: If enabled, yes. Whitelist the plug MAC.

title: Plug Offline
shortDescription: Plug lost contact with the Kasa cloud.
fullDescription:
An offline plug may still be powered but cannot reach the cloud service. Router reboots, ISP outages, or plug firmware hangs all produce this state.

Power-cycle the plug by unplugging for 30 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug, wait 30 s, plug back in.

faq.q: Does local control work while offline?
faq.a: Yes, if the phone is on the same LAN.

title: Firmware Update Failure
shortDescription: OTA update did not complete successfully.
fullDescription:
OTA failures are typically caused by poor Wi-Fi during download. The plug usually reverts to the previous firmware automatically.

Retry the update with the plug close to the router.

fixSteps.title: Retry update
fixSteps.instruction: Kasa app > device settings > Firmware Update.

faq.q: Is the plug bricked after a failed update?
faq.a: Almost never - it rolls back automatically.

title: Schedule Did Not Run
shortDescription: Programmed on/off schedule failed to execute.
fullDescription:
Schedules rely on the plug's internal clock syncing with NTP. Plugs offline at sync time or with wrong timezone will miss events.

Ensure the plug is online and timezone is correct in settings.
symptoms: Plug didn't switch at scheduled time

fixSteps.title: Reboot plug
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle to force clock sync.

faq.a: Yes, if the plug has the schedule cached and clock is synced.

title: App Does Not Discover Plug
shortDescription: Already-configured plug missing from the app.
fullDescription:
This can happen after reinstalling Kasa, changing accounts, or when local discovery is blocked by client isolation on the router.

Log into the original account or disable AP isolation.
symptoms: Plug still works with old account

fixSteps.title: Confirm account
fixSteps.instruction: Sign into the account used during original setup.

fixSteps.title: Disable AP isolation
fixSteps.instruction: In router > Wireless > disable Client Isolation.

videoSearchQuery: Kasa app not finding device fix

faq.q: Can I move a plug to a new account?
faq.a: Factory reset the plug and add it fresh to the new account.

title: Relay Clicks Repeatedly
fullDescription:
Repeated relay clicks usually indicate a faulty relay, low line voltage, or a stuck firmware loop. If the plug is under warranty, request an RMA.

Disconnect any load and reset to factory to see if the clicking stops.

fixSteps.title: Remove load
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug anything from the Kasa, leave plug in outlet alone.

fixSteps.title: Request RMA
fixSteps.instruction: If clicking persists, contact TP-Link support.

whenToCallPro: If under warranty request replacement; do not open the plug.

faq.q: Safe to keep using a clicking plug?
faq.a: No, unplug it and request replacement.

title: Voice Assistant Cannot Control Plug
shortDescription: Alexa or Google Home cannot switch the plug.
fullDescription:
Voice control relies on the Kasa skill/integration. When the plug is renamed, moved to a new account, or the skill is disabled, voice commands fail.

Disable and re-enable the Kasa skill, then re-discover devices.

fixSteps.title: Re-link skill
fixSteps.instruction: Alexa app > Skills > Kasa > Disable > Re-enable, then discover devices.

videoSearchQuery: Kasa plug alexa not working fix

faq.a: Voice uses the current name; after renaming, say the new name.
